title: Bulls and Cows
summary: In the Bulls and Cows game, you provide a hint to your friend's guess by indicating the number of bulls (correct digits in the correct positions) and cows (correct digits in the wrong positions).
statement: In the Bulls and Cows game, you provide a hint to your friend's guess by indicating the number of bulls (correct digits in the correct positions) and cows (correct digits in the wrong positions). The hint format is 'xAyB', where x is the count of bulls and y is the count of cows.
constraints: secret and guess contain the same 1–1000 number of decimal digits; repeated digits and leading zeroes are allowed.
Return a hint formatted as xAyB. A bull is an equal digit at the same index; a cow is a remaining equal digit matched at a different index. Each occurrence can be used at most once.
known_wrong_solutions:
def bulls_and_cows(secret, guess):
    bulls = sum(left == right for left, right in zip(secret, guess))
    shared = len(set(secret) & set(guess))
    return f"{bulls}A{shared - bulls}B"
def bulls_and_cows(secret, guess):
    bulls = sum(left == right for left, right in zip(secret, guess))
    cows = sum(character in secret for index, character in enumerate(guess) if character != secret[index])
    return f"{bulls}A{cows}B"
hints: Separate same-position matches before counting misplaced digits.
For each digit, the number of cows is the smaller unmatched frequency in secret and guess.
Scan the strings once into two ten-slot frequency arrays, skipping bull positions, then sum per-digit minima.
Removing bulls first prevents one occurrence from being counted both as a bull and as a cow.
editorial: A same-index match is reserved as a bull. Every remaining occurrence of digit d can participate in at most one cow, so exactly min(unmatched_secret[d], unmatched_guess[d]) copies match. Ten fixed counters make the scan linear and constant-space. The independent oracle intersects full Counters, subtracting the already identified bulls from the total shared multiplicity.

tests.explanation: Digit 8 is the one bull. Digits 1, 0, and 7 match at different positions, giving 1A3B.
The second digit is a bull and only one remaining 1 can be matched as a cow, so duplicates are capped at 1A1B.
